chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Homayry said: He narrated to me Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboob, from Abu Ayoob al-Khizaz, from Abu Ubaydat al-Haza'a, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

A believer is one whose pleasure would not lead him into sin and wrongful deeds. A believer is one whose anger would not lead him away from rightful statements. A believer is one whose power would not force him to act unjustly and to acquire what doesn’t rightfully belong to him.
ai.seo_question: What are the three characteristics of a perfect believer according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) outlines the triad of moral equilibrium that defines perfect faith: maintaining justice in contentment, adhering to truth in anger, and avoiding transgression when endowed with power. This teaching emphasizes that true *Iman* is not merely belief but a stable character state where external circumstances do not distort one's ethical conduct, a concept central to Shia ethical theology (*Akhlaq*).

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-65 Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Abdullah ibn Ja’far al-Homayry quoted on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Mahboob, on the authority of Abi Ayoob al-Khizaz, on the authority of Abi Ubaydat al-Haza’a that Abi Ja’far al-Baqir (MGB) said, “

A believer is one whose pleasure would not lead him into sin and wrongful deeds. A believer is one whose anger would not lead him away from rightful statements. A believer is one whose power would not force him to act unjustly and to acquire what doesn’t rightfully belong to him.”
